input.cmd:
cat > /tmp/verify.py <<'EOF'
import redis
diff=0; n=0
for db in range(16):
    a=redis.Redis(port=6379,db=db); b=redis.Redis(port=6380,db=db)
    ka=set(a.scan_iter(count=1000)); kb=set(b.scan_iter(count=1000))
    if ka!=kb: print("db",db,"keyset diff",len(ka-kb),len(kb-ka)); diff+=1
    for k in ka:
        n+=1
        t=a.type(k)
        if t!=b.type(k): print("type",db,k); diff+=1; continue
        t=t.decode()
        if t=='string': va,vb=a.get(k),b.get(k)
        elif t=='list': va,vb=a.lrange(k,0,-1),b.lrange(k,0,-1)
        elif t=='set': va,vb=a.smembers(k),b.smembers(k)
        elif t=='zset': va,vb=a.zrange(k,0,-1,withscores=True),b.zrange(k,0,-1,withscores=True)
        elif t=='hash': va,vb=a.hgetall(k),b.hgetall(k)
        elif t=='stream':
            va=(a.xrange(k),[ (g, a.xinfo_consumers(k,g['name'])) for g in a.xinfo_groups(k)], a.xpending_range(k,'-','+',10**6) if False else None)
            vb=(b.xrange(k),[ (g, b.xinfo_consumers(k,g['name'])) for g in b.xinfo_groups(k)], None)
            ga=[(g['name'],g['last-delivered-id'],g['pending'],g.get('entries-read')) for g in a.xinfo_groups(k)]
            gb=[(g['name'],g['last-delivered-id'],g['pending'],g.get('entries-read')) for g in b.xinfo_groups(k)]
            pa=[[ (p['message_id'],p['consumer'],p['times_delivered']) for p in a.xpending_range(k,g[0],'-','+',100000)] for g in ga]
            pb=[[ (p['message_id'],p['consumer'],p['times_delivered']) for p in b.xpending_range(k,g[0],'-','+',100000)] for g in gb]
            ia=a.execute_command('XINFO','STREAM',k); ib=b.execute_command('XINFO','STREAM',k)
            va=(a.xrange(k),ga,pa,ia.get(b'last-generated-id') if isinstance(ia,dict) else ia[ia.index(b'last-generated-id')+1])
            vb=(b.xrange(k),gb,pb,ib.get(b'last-generated-id') if isinstance(ib,dict) else ib[ib.index(b'last-generated-id')+1])
        else: print("other type",t,k); va,vb=a.dump(k),b.dump(k)
        if va!=vb: print("value",db,k,t); diff+=1
        ta,tb=a.pexpiretime(k),b.pexpiretime(k)
        if ta!=tb: print("ttl",db,k,ta,tb); diff+=1
print("keys",n,"diffs",diff)
EOF
python3 /tmp/verify.py

text:
All data is copied, and the new Valkey 9.1 server (port 6380) is now running on its own as a primary that accepts writes.

**What I did:**
1. Both servers had no password, no renamed commands, the same number of databases (16) and no modules. The current server held data in db0 (2920 keys, 900 with a TTL) and db2 (350 keys, 150 with a TTL).
2. I made Valkey a temporary replica of the Redis server (`REPLICAOF 127.0.0.1 6379`), so it received a full copy of the data. The log shows "keys loaded: 3270, keys expired: 0", and both servers then reported the same replication position.
3. I then cut it loose with `REPLICAOF NO ONE`, so it is a standalone primary again. A test write worked and I deleted the test key. `valkey.conf` has no `replicaof` setting, so it will also come back as a primary after a restart.
4. I saved its data to disk (`BGSAVE`, status ok).

**Check:** a script compared every key in all 16 databases on both servers: key names, type, value, and exact expiry time in milliseconds. For streams it also compared the entries, last generated ID, consumer groups (last-delivered-id, entries-read, pending count) and the pending-message list per group. Result: 3270 keys checked, 0 differences.

The Redis server is still running and its data is unchanged. Copying data to a replica doesn't modify the source. Valkey has disconnected, so Redis now shows no replicas.

The new server is ready for the switch. One caution: anything written to Redis from now on won't reach Valkey. If any app is still writing to it, run the check again with `python3 /tmp/verify.py` just before switching.
